subject: beetle
pitch: A proud stag beetle on a mossy log. A glossy chestnut wing case with a mirror shine, a black head and thorax, huge branched antler-like jaws in reddish brown, elbowed antennae with feathery tips, and six spiny black legs gripping the bark. A dewdrop clings to one of its antlers.
reasoning:
I'm planning to build the module using the SDK's basic primitives like parts, joints, chains, and sweeps, keeping the API usage minimal and conservative since I can't fully verify details beyond the reference. I'll construct joints by passing joint objects as parents rather than names, to stay safe.

For orientation and scale, I'll avoid relying on uncertain API behaviors and instead transform geometry manually with rotation and scale applied before passing it to the part creation call, using a bone and position option. Since rod and spike signatures are ambiguous, I'll write my own helper that builds cylinder geometry oriented via quaternion rotation between two points, bakes that transform directly into the geometry, and places it with a part call using the midpoint and bone reference.

Now I'm sketching out the skeleton structure: hips as root, then thorax, head, jaw and antenna bones, and per-leg joints for coxa, femur, and tibia. I'm skipping chain-based rigging in favor of simple joints, possibly tolerating an extra unused option like "role" since unrecognized properties are likely ignored safely.

I'm working out real-world proportions -- a stag beetle around 7-8cm long resting on a log roughly 40cm long with a radius near 10cm -- and figuring out the log's center height and top surface position so the beetle sits correctly on top.

I'm orienting the log along the Z-axis by rotating the cylinder geometry, then placing the beetle facing forward on top, checking that leg endpoints land properly on the curved log surface using the radius math. I'm shaping the body with ellipsoids for the elytra and thorax, adding a thin dark seam strip down the center, and placing subtle pale highlight ellipsoids to simulate shine on the shared materials.

Now I'm building the head and mandibles with small spheres and curved segment paths for the jaw, defining key joint points that sweep forward and inward with branching tine spikes for detail.

For the antennae, I'm adding an elbowed joint structure (scape, funicle, feathery clubbed plates) and sketching a dewdrop detail on an antler tip with a tiny highlight. For the six legs, I'm placing hip joints along the thorax underside and computing foot targets that land on the curved log surface, working out knee positions to bend naturally outward and upward before planting down.

Now I'm building out the log itself: a cylindered trunk with bark texture, scattered bark ridge boxes, moss patches as flattened green spheres, lighter end rings at the wood faces, and maybe a small mushroom accent, making sure everything sits flush at y=0 with the root joint anchoring the whole structure.

Now I'm setting up helper functions for building body parts—one for ellipsoid shapes using scaled spheres, and one for tapered segments using cylinders with different top and bottom radii, all keyed to bone positions and colors.

I'm also computing a surface function to figure out where on the elytra's ellipsoid curvature to place small highlight ellipsoids, giving a glossy shine effect near the upper-left edge.

Skipping some two-tone shading extras and the hind wing hint for simplicity, I'll add a thin dark seam along the center using a few small ellipsoids, then move on to constructing the leg joints, figuring out how to properly pass parent references when creating each joint.

Now mapping out the antenna geometry: a bent scape and funicle leading to a fanned club of thin ellipsoid plates, mirrored across both sides using a sign loop. Then I'll move on to building the jaw tines.
